query: For refractory high-entropy alloys intended for structural use under extreme-temperature conditions, what single intervention could improve high-temperature oxygen resistance? State one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to the untreated alloy, defines the temperature, atmosphere, and exposure conditions under which it should work, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment with a clear result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Aluminum oxide (Al2O3) reinforcement particles can improve high-temperature oxygen resistance in refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) by forming a protective oxide layer.
generation.material_initial_state: Refractory high-entropy alloy (RHEA) in its as-cast or as-sintered state
generation.intervention: Addition of aluminum oxide (Al2O3) reinforcement particles
generation.conditions: High-temperature conditions (above 500°C) in an oxygen-rich atmosphere
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a protective Al2O3 oxide layer on the surface of the RHEA
generation.mechanism: The Al2O3 oxide layer acts as a barrier to oxygen diffusion, reducing oxidation and improving high-temperature oxygen resistance
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved high-temperature oxygen resistance and reduced oxidation of the RHEA
generation.baseline: Untreated RHEA without Al2O3 reinforcement particles
generation.boundary: Temperature range: 500°C to 1000°C, Atmosphere: Oxygen-rich, Exposure conditions: Static or dynamic
generation.uncertainty: The optimal amount and distribution of Al2O3 reinforcement particles, as well as the potential effects of other alloying elements on the oxide layer formation and properties

falsification_experiment.design: Compare the high-temperature oxygen resistance of RHEA samples with and without Al2O3 reinforcement particles
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the RHEA sample without Al2O3 reinforcement particles shows equal or better high-temperature oxygen resistance than the sample with Al2O3 reinforcement particles, the hypothesis is falsified

Question: How can the compressive strength of the NbMoCrTiAl refractory high-entropy alloy be improved for high-temperature structural applications while maintaining oxidation resistance?. System: NbMoCrTiAl high entropy alloy matrix with in-situ formed TiC and Al2O3 reinforcement particles. Processing: High energy planetary ball milling for 39 h at 300 rpm with stearic acid as process control agent, followed by spark plasma sintering (SPS) at 1700 °C under 30 MPa axial pressure for 30 min. Test conditions: Room temperature compression tests at a strain rate of 10^-3 s^-1 on cylindrical specimens (4 mm diameter, 6 mm height).
